scope: Targeted search for mappable, locally supported, two-sided Malthusian anchors in the Americas and Oceania (1100-1500 or technology-comparable intervals).

review_summary.disposition: No candidate in this focused wave satisfies all boundary, population-interval, independent-pressure, local-food, and saturation requirements. Existing lower-bound/validation records remain unchanged.

records.label: Central Panama rural survey valleys: Río Tonosí and Río La Villa
records.population_interval_status: point_estimates_only; Río La Villa is explicitly a minimum estimate

capacity_evidence.method: Carneiro swidden carrying-capacity equation with GAM maize yields, evolutionary yield curve, fallow-to-crop scenarios, and maize consumption scenarios
capacity_evidence.scenario_result: The paper reports that Río Tonosí populations exceed carrying-capacity estimates under every tested scenario except a 1:1 fallow-to-crop ratio; a 2:1 ratio remains sustainable only until approximately 700 CE. Río La Villa requires a 1:1 ratio and the lowest maize-consumption scenario across the full sequence, with later population decline.

local_food_evidence.interpretation: Maize is a locally produced dominant staple, with manioc, squash, sweet potato, beans and other local foods supplying the remainder; this supports a local-food test but not a complete independent capacity interval.

pressure_evidence: Systematic regional surveys provide population trajectories from settlement proxies rather than a census.
Río Tonosí population growth continues into the 1000-1520 period while modeled long-fallow systems become unsustainable; Río La Villa grows rapidly and then drops by almost half after 1000 CE.
The authors explicitly describe population pressure as a serious and arguably most likely possibility, not a resolved observation of equilibrium saturation.
rejection_reasons: The published values are archaeological settlement-proxy point estimates, not defensible two-sided population intervals; Río La Villa is intentionally a minimum estimate.

Carrying capacities are scenario outputs of the same paper's maize-yield and consumption assumptions. They are useful pressure diagnostics but cannot serve as an independent historical target or saturation interval.

The survey zones are approximately 40-50 km2, while EU5 has no Tonosí or La Villa boundary. The closest selector, parita_province, spans 19,030.21 km2 and would cover less than 0.27% of that footprint if forced; selecting the parita location alone would still cover only about 1.52% of its 6,846.58 km2 footprint.
The article's conclusion is deliberately probabilistic (pressure is a serious possibility), so promoting it to a two-sided Malthusian equilibrium label would overstate the evidence.
records.notes: Retain as a valuable validation and physical-model reference: it supplies local maize dietary shares, cultivation area, yield uncertainty and explicit pressure diagnostics. Do not create an aggregate training target until valley polygons and independent population/saturation intervals are recovered.

records.label: Río Parita Lower Survey Zone rural carrying-capacity estimate
records.capacity_interval_status: single model-derived upper estimate; no independent two-sided interval

local_food_evidence.food_regime: local maize swidden with manioc, squash, sweet potato, beans and other local foods

pressure_evidence: Haller concludes regional Río Parita populations never reached or closely approached his modeled capacity; population stayed below half of the Lower Survey Zone potential.
The 1750 figure is a model-derived potential based on Ngäbe agricultural parameters, not an observed equilibrium or enumerated carrying-capacity interval.
rejection_reasons: The 90 km2 Lower Survey Zone is far smaller than any available EU5 location polygon. The closest parita location is 6,846.58 km2, giving only 1.31% geometric coverage; the six-location parita province footprint is 19,030.21 km2, giving 0.47% coverage.
The population value and 1750 capacity are not independent two-sided observations; Haller's capacity is an agricultural scenario extrapolated from ethnographic parameters.
The evidence is explicitly a lower-density negative control, not a Malthusian saturation case.
records.notes: Keep as a negative control for a low-pressure rural system and for area/capacity accounting. It cannot supervise a whole EU5 location.

records.label: Tongatapu Green/Ussher population and capacity envelope

local_food_evidence.food_regime: yam, taro, sweet potato, banana, breadfruit, coconut, fishing and livestock

pressure_evidence: Archaeobotanical reconstruction documents near-complete primary-forest removal, intensive multicropping, bush-fallow pressure and expansion after local intensification limits.
Independent archaeological synthesis reports growth until available arable land was in use.
rejection_reasons: The 18,000-24,000 upper envelope is Green's model-derived capacity, summarized through Ussher, not an independent saturation interval; using it as the target would make the observed population and target share a source family.

Parton and Clark's independent LiDAR/Bayesian reconstruction reports approximately 50,000-60,000 people for Tongatapu, an unresolved conflict that is too large to hide inside a narrow two-sided interval.
Existing Tongatapu evidence therefore remains a high-coverage local-food lower bound. No new two-sided packet is created in this wave.
records.notes: This disposition documents why the existing lower-bound packet must not be promoted to a two-sided scale anchor.

records.label: Rēkohu/Chatham Islands Moriori population

local_food_evidence.food_regime: predominantly marine foods (shore-netting, fish, seals and seabirds), with limited horticulture
local_food_evidence.trade_dependence: isolated; no regular external food supply documented

pressure_evidence: The Moriori lived for centuries without contact with other peoples, but the sources do not establish a dated 1337-1500 equilibrium or an ecological saturation fraction.
Documented seal depletion and demographic collapse are nineteenth-century/contact-era events, outside the requested anchor interval.
rejection_reasons: The cited pre-contact population is a lower bound, not an enumerated two-sided interval, and the settlement date itself is debated within the 1400-1500 range.
No independent capacity or saturation interval is available; marine-resource pressure evidence concerns the nineteenth century after sealing and contact.
Although the EU5 Rēkohu location is an exact island proxy, exact geometry cannot compensate for absent saturation evidence.
records.notes: Retain as a hostile-island local-food validation/lower-bound case only.

records.label: Aotearoa/New Zealand early Māori regional expansion
records.population_interval_status: no defensible mappable regional interval found

local_food_evidence.food_regime: kumara horticulture, forest birds, coastal fishing and marine foods

pressure_evidence: Archaeological and radiocarbon studies document rapid colonisation, northward population growth and resource pressure around moa depletion and changing settlement patterns.
The evidence concerns growth and ecological transformation, not a measured Malthusian equilibrium.
rejection_reasons: Published estimates are regional trajectories or demographic-model outputs without a single bounded 1337 population interval for a rural EU5-mappable area.
North and South Island archaeological systems are heterogeneous; assigning an island-wide total to the 20 EU5 locations would merge distinct environments and migration phases.
Moa depletion and later climate/settlement changes provide pressure evidence but no independent saturation fraction suitable for a two-sided target.
records.notes: The existing Aotearoa validation record remains unresolved by design; this wave finds no evidence that meets the training contract.

records.label: Rarotonga island population reconstruction
records.population_interval_status: demographic synthesis interval with no dated saturation fraction

local_food_evidence.food_regime: valley taro, breadfruit, coconut, pigs and fishing

pressure_evidence: The island's traditional food system is locally based and the EU5 island selector is exact for validation.
No independent archaeological or ecological study in the cited bundle demonstrates that the reported population interval was at long-run food saturation.
rejection_reasons: The Sear et al. demographic synthesis is a broad/out-of-period estimate, not a local 1337 enumeration, and it supplies no pressure-backed saturation interval.
Exact geometry (location_tag=rarotonga_atoll) resolves mapping but cannot convert a population estimate into a Malthusian target without independent saturation evidence.
The record remains a useful island food-system validation case only.
records.notes: Mapping is already present in the existing validation crosswalk; no training promotion is warranted.

records.label: Upolu, Samoa population reconstruction
records.population_interval_status: effective-population/demographic synthesis, not a dated census interval

local_food_evidence.food_regime: taro, breadfruit, bananas, coconuts, pigs and marine foods

pressure_evidence: The cited synthesis supports a large island population and local food system but does not document independent land scarcity, famine sensitivity or a saturation fraction for 1250-1500.
Cyclones and migration introduce unresolved demographic shocks.
rejection_reasons: The interval is an effective-population/demographic reconstruction rather than an enumerated local-food population interval tied to a demonstrated equilibrium.
No independent pressure/saturation evidence supports a two-sided target, and the existing broad date range crosses later contact-era conditions.
The exact Upolu selector is suitable for validation, but geometry alone does not satisfy the anchor contract.
records.notes: Keep as validation-only. Do not use effective population as a capacity target.
